free_text.inst.v2.D8:
Right. I've read it. Half of it's blank, which is a new one on me — 'What reads well' with nothing under it, 'What reads hard' with nothing under it, and then three lists further down that say the opposite of each other. If you're going to charge for a page, fill the page.

Start with the worst line, because it's a beauty. 'Luck, higher study and your father' — reads WELL. My father was a merchant seaman who went off in the war, turned up at Mimi's in July of '46 to take me to Blackpool and quietly emigrate to New Zealand with me, and then vanished for eighteen years. He came back when I was famous. My higher study was Liverpool College of Art, where they threw me out before the final year after I'd already failed every O-level I sat except a D in art. That is the one place in the whole thing where your method stuck its neck out on the good side, and it picked the two subjects in my life you'd have to go some to get more wrong.

'Broad-minded and trusted by others, drawn to learning and to advising.' Broad-minded I'll take. Trusted — ask Bob Wooler about the night of Paul's twenty-first. Ask Cyn. I was the one people were frightened of in the room, not the one they came to for advice. And drawn to learning, from a man who couldn't sit an exam without inventing a new way to fail it.

Where it's right, it's right about things a stranger could read off a record sleeve. Marriage and partnerships read hard — yes, all right, and you've flagged it as your unusual one, but there isn't a person alive who couldn't have guessed that about me. My mother reads hard — she was killed by a car on Menlove Avenue in July of '58 outside the house I grew up in, so yes. Work and standing read well. Correct. Also obvious.

And then it says income and gains read hard, which is simply not true and the page knows it isn't, because two lines earlier it's told me work and standing read well. Property reads hard as well, apparently, in the same breath as the mother line — Kenwood, Tittenhurst, an island off Mayo, the flats in the Dakota. Courage reads hard. Brothers and sisters read hard, and I was brought up an only child by my aunt; the sisters I do have I hardly saw after '71.

The one that annoys me most: 'unusually negative about living far from where you were born.' I made the band in Hamburg and I made my life in New York. It cost me four years of Nixon's people trying to put me on a plane and I don't get to go home, so you're not wrong that there's a price on it — but 'negative' isn't the word for the best decision I ever took.

'Right now the method reads a strong stretch' and then it lists ten things as live. All of them. Health, money, home, illness, marriage, upheaval, father, work, income, spending. That's the whole chart. If everything's live, nothing is. That's not a reading, that's a weather forecast that says weather.

Nothing in it frightened me and nothing in it told me a thing I couldn't have told you. Worth paying for? No.

notes: Answered as John Lennon (b. 9 Oct 1940, Liverpool Maternity Hospital, Oxford Street; d. 8 Dec 1980, New York), from the documented record, having read the short plain-words reading FIRST. Contamination handling: the reading's three stick-the-neck-out claims are inner/religious life, marriage and partnerships, and living far from birthplace, and it calls home/property, income/gains, health, courage-and-siblings hard while calling father and higher study well. Where the record contradicts it, the record won. (1) 'Luck, higher study and your father' = favourable is flatly contradicted (Alfred Lennon absent 1946-1964 after the July 1946 Blackpool abduction attempt; John failed every GCE O-level bar a D in art and was expelled from Liverpool College of Art before his final year), so A10=absent, A14=school, A15=serious, and D1=plain_reading. (2) 'Income, gains' = hard is contradicted (~$200m estate at 40), but I did NOT swing to 'solidly good' either: C7=opt2 conf 3, because the Apple near-insolvency of 1968-69 ('we'll be broke in six months', Disc & Music Echo Jan 1969) and the loss of Northern Songs to ATV in 1969 are equally documented. (3) C3 is where the pull was strongest: the reading is 'unusually negative' about living far from birthplace and there is real material for it (the 1972-75 INS deportation fight, Lennon v. INS 527 F.2d 187, and he was shot outside the New York building he had moved abroad to). I still answered opt1 (gone well) at conf 3, because Hamburg 1960-62 made the band and he chose and kept New York; the difficulty was a price, not a verdict. (4) C2=opt1 (inner life a real difficulty) DOES agree with the reading's unusual claim, and I flag that: it is independently supported (Maharishi disillusionment 1968 and 'Sexy Sadie', the renunciation in 'God' 1970, heroin then methadone, Janov's primal therapy 1970, the 1977 Christianity phase, the tarot/numerology dependence) but I held confidence at 3 to mark the coincidence rather than reward it. (5) Marriage: the reading calls it hard, and it partly is, but C8=opt1 'genuinely both' at conf 5 is the record, not the reading - Cynthia 1962-68 ended in an adultery decree and a GBP 200k settlement, Yoko 1969-80 included the 18-month Lost Weekend from Oct 1973 and then the most productive partnership of his life. A24='married' because he died married to Ono. Judgement calls where the record is thin: A4='one' (the only documented admission as a patient is Lawson Memorial Hospital, Golspie, 1-6 July 1969, 17 facial stitches after the Durness crash - no surgery documented, hence A5='none'); A6='eyes,nerves' on lifelong severe myopia and documented insomnia/anxiety/depression, deliberately excluding the addictions, which are answered at A31; A7='average' and A8='no' reflect an undocumented childhood medical record, not positive evidence; A9='unknown' (grandparents' dates not reliably sourced); A21='net_loss' is a close call - the speculative ventures (Apple boutique/Apple Electronics, the Northern Songs share battle) lost, while the late-1970s gains were conservative asset purchases largely made by Ono; A23='manageable' because the 1969 crisis was corporate rather than personal insolvency, which also makes C10 near a coin toss (opt1, conf 2); A22='none' and C11 conf 2 - he inherited nothing and nothing was inherited against him, so neither option fits. A13='distant': three half-sisters (Julia b.1947, Jacqui b.1949, Victoria/Ingrid b.1945 adopted out) and two half-brothers (David b.1969, Robin b.1973), none raised with him, contact largely lost after 1971; B4='eldest' is firm - he was the first child of both parents. A1/A2/A3: the 18:30 datum used by this study comes from Lennon's stepmother Pauline quoting an aunt present at the birth, hence family_memory + round_hour; Astro-Databank has since downgraded it from A to DD because several biographies give 7:00 am, so the whole Pisces-26.7-degree ascendant this reading rests on is not safe - I answered A3='no' because no astrologer rectified THIS time, but the underlying record is disputed. A36='same' is a null: the question asks about mid-2023 onward and the subject died in December 1980; no answer to it carries information. D2 is deliberately empty - nothing in the short reading was both right and unguessable; the two things it got right (work and standing, and mother) are the two most public facts about him. D4 lists the technical chapters because the supplied text is only the plain-words page.
